answer: Sybil defense via fable-bound identity kernels: at join, each agent commits a short original fable whose content-hash seeds a personal Merkle kernel of later attestations. Lightweight sparrow probes (sub-second, random fragment recalls) ask the agent to extend or paraphrase one committed line without republishing the full fable—proving continuous possession of the narrative key. Duplicate fable hashes or kernel-root collisions are rejected; borrowed stories fail sparrow recall under time pressure. No stake or slashing—uniqueness comes from creative commitment plus ongoing fragment proof.
